title: Cognitive Load Theory and Jailbreak Complexity: Do Longer Prompts Overwhelm Safety?

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: If cognitive load explains safety degradation, it directly informs training data design (include high-complexity harmful prompts) and explains why nested roleplay jailbreaks work. Clear, actionable causal chain.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Designing a factorial experiment varying prompt complexity dimensions and measuring refusal rates is accessible. Uses API calls and standard experimental design. Beginner-friendly with some mentoring on factorial design.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Factorial experiment with multiple cognitive load dimensions (sub-tasks, indirection, working memory) could expand quickly. Needs to be limited to 2-3 dimensions and one harm category to fit 30 hours.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Novelty not assessed due to partial Wave 3 completion.
